items.title: Vance 2028 Is Here
items.description: J. D. Vance’s strategy, since he became the Republican Party’s vice-presidential nominee in 2024, has been for President Trump to coronate him as his successor. “Donald Trump will ultimately decide who’s going to be the Republican nominee,” Vance told Sean Spicer last month, neatly excising the primary electorate from the decision matrix. Yet the midterm elections indicate the existence of a market among Republican voters for a 2028 presidential candidate who will distance their campaign from the current administration’s failures. Vance wants to be that Republican, but without forfeiting Trump’s support. How does he manage to do both? Blame everything on the Iran war. That is what Vance shrewdly, if disingenuously, has done. In a lengthy post on X , the vice president fully conceded that his party had been routed, and that “many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.” You often see analysts describing the 2024 Republican presidential electorate as “Trump voters,” but Vance understandably avoided this shorthand. [ Read: The simple message that produced a Democratic landslide ] He reduced the disaster to a single cause, writing: “The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.” This argument has several advantages. First, it is partially correct. The Iran war has been a political debacle, both because it violated Trump’s oft-stated promise to avoid quagmires and because it drove up the cost of fuel and other goods. Second, and of equal importance, Trump likely agrees with this critique. The president has been publicly blaming Iran for months, while defensively insisting that the cost has been minor, temporary (the conflict has been two weeks away from ending since it began), and necessary to avoid nuclear cataclysm. In a Fox News interview last night, Trump insisted, “We actually have the greatest economy,” but “because of the gasoline price, people don’t see it as much as they would have without it. And the gasoline was caused by Iran.” Donald Trump Jr. quickly shared Vance’s post, commenting, “Every word of this is 💯💯💯,” stamping the royal family’s quasi-official imprimatur on Vance’s concession. Third, Vance’s argument aims to box out his most likely rival, Secretary of State Marco Rubio. If the war is the problem, then why would anybody prefer a Cabinet official whose entire job is foreign policy? Rubio is a well-known foreign-policy hawk, and blaming the hawks for snookering Trump into a mistake implicates the Rubio wing of the party for the midterm debacle. Fourth, Vance ignores every other way Trump dismantled the 2024 Republican coalition. Tariffs? Mass deportation? Corruption? The gilded-palace binge? A domestic agenda focused on cutting taxes for the rich, while throwing millions of low-income Americans off their health insurance and food stamps? Trump is not willing to cop to mistakes on any of them, and Vance either justified or enthusiastically supported all of these errors, anyway. In his X post, Vance specifically tried to refute Republican critics who (correctly) believe that the administration’s ironfisted approach to immigration enforcement alienated Latino voters who had expected a narrower approach focused on deporting criminals. “Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty,” Vance wrote. “I’m open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you.” “Amnesty” is not the only alternative to Stephen Miller’s plan of deploying hastily trained masked agents and encouraging them to use the roughest tactics. But amnesty was a feature of an immigration-reform plan that Rubio briefly supported during Barack Obama’s second term, a historical fact that might explain Vance’s eagerness to revive the concept—as an epithet against his factional rivals. Vance’s post asserts that a pollster told him that disgruntled Trump voters—sorry, Trump/ Vance voters—would “come back on our team” if the administration did four things: 1) End the war 2) Focus on cost of living/inflation 3) Put America First 4) Change our relationship to Israel. From a certain point of view that is especially prominent on the online right, those four things can be reduced to one thing: Trump has to stop letting Israel manipulate him into foreign wars, and instead focus on making Americans rich. Conveniently for Vance, Trump appears open to this critique, having blurted out on Fox News yesterday that he now favors phasing out American aid to Israel. [ David Frum: Things are going to get ugly ] Vance is right to imply that Israel helped persuade Trump to go to war with Iran. But Israel’s advocacy is not the only reason the Strait of Hormuz has been closed. Trump has argued on and off for attacking Iran since it emerged as an American bête noir during the hostage crisis that began in 1979, when Trump’s short list of immutable beliefs about the world first formed. Trump also seemed to drop his inhibitions about the use of military force after the kidnapping of Nicolás Maduro left him giddy with power. Blaming all of the administration’s domestic failures on the Iran war, while subtly pointing the finger at Benjamin Netanyahu for tricking the president into it, would seem to offer Vance the shortest and straightest path to holding together the MAGA coalition and his place within it. The Trump presidency is working perfectly well, and the only slight course correction required is to recommit to “America First” principles . Who among us might lead the MAGA movement into this new future of Trumpism-without-war? And without veering away from Trump’s militarized immigration strategy, or acknowledging the ongoing orgy of corruption and abuse of power? Only one man.

items.title: The End of the Trump Era
items.description: Well, that was weird. The Donald Trump era, I mean. It’s over now. It ended yesterday when voters handed control of both houses of Congress to the Democratic Party, along with a clear set of instructions: Stop the madness. Be honest. Be competent. Be normal. Be nice. Trump will still be president for another two years, of course, and it is unimaginable that he will go gently into lame-duck irrelevance. But the Republican Party, or what is left of it, surely must realize that the late Senator Lindsey Graham from South Carolina was right—though a decade premature—when in 2016 he warned : “If we nominate Trump we will get destroyed.......and we will deserve it.” Graham’s Senate seat will be occupied for the next six years by the pediatrician Annie Andrews, a Democrat. The last time a Democrat held that seat was in 1964, just before Strom Thurmond changed parties and became a Republican. Trump’s handpicked GOP candidate—Darline Graham, the late senator’s sister—lost by coming across to voters as utterly clueless. Trump used his control of his party to defeat Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina in his Republican primary; his seat will now be filled by Democrat Roy Cooper. Trump did the same to Senator John Cornyn of Texas; his seat went to Democrat James Talarico, who beat Trump’s chosen candidate—the scandal-plagued Ken Paxton—by more than 1 million votes. Texas Governor Greg Abbott was collateral damage, losing to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who will be the state’s first Latina governor. In fact, Democrats swept all of the statewide offices up for grabs in Texas, from governor and lieutenant governor down to railroad commissioner. [ Helen Lewis: A night of pure Trumpenfreude ] With Trump’s guidance, Republicans lost a Senate seat in reliably red Iowa. They lost a Senate seat in Kansas, which had elected its previous Democratic senator in 1930. As of this writing, Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith of Mississippi trails Democrat Scott Colom, a Black district attorney, by 65 votes. In Mississippi . This goes far beyond the usual midterm setback for the party that holds the White House. It is as thorough a repudiation as we have seen since the post-Watergate 1974 midterms. Just as that election was a referendum on Richard Nixon, this one was a referendum on Trump. And the rebuke was about more than gas prices. Voters said no to the corruption and self-dealing of the Trump era. In the exit poll conducted for a consortium of news organizations by the polling firm SSRS, 90 percent of respondents said that government corruption was either “crucial” or “a major factor” in how they voted in House races. Clearly that concern was expressed in other contests as well—notably, the resounding defeat of Paxton, whose past includes indictment on securities-fraud charges and impeachment by the GOP-controlled Texas House of Representatives. Voters said no to the Trump era’s incompetence. Almost every Democratic candidate ran on a policy of quickly ending the Iran war, which Trump blundered into and has no idea how to exit. Asked about her views on foreign policy in a debate, Darline Graham said that she really didn’t have any. There are Republican members of Congress who do have informed, nuanced views about foreign policy. But they were afraid to say what they knew about the Iran debacle or the shattering of our nation’s most important alliances or this administration’s unthinkable coziness with Vladimir Putin, because they did not want to face Trump’s ire. Some of those who remained silent are soon-to-be-former members of Congress. Voters said no to the Trump-era ethos of outrageousness for its own sake. Trump, the former star of The Apprentice , has always scripted his presidency as if it were a reality show: What matters isn’t doing what’s right; it’s attracting eyeballs, dominating the news cycle, drawing attention. That surely is what the GOP candidate Vivek Ramaswamy thought he was doing when he aired that shocking ad—praised by Trump and Vice President Vance—in which Ohio Democrat Amy Acton’s mother accused her of being a liar. Ramaswamy apparently did not care that the mother had fled the state with her husband after he was indicted for allegedly sexually abusing Acton when she was 12. Voters in Ohio, another red state, cared a lot. Acton, and not Ramaswamy, will be the next governor. [ Jonathan Lemire: Repudiation ] Voters also said no to what might be the Trump era’s defining characteristic: gratuitous cruelty. Under the malign influence of White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, the administration has sent armed and masked federal agents into neighborhoods across the country, snatching immigrants from their homes and workplaces and sending them to detention centers for rapid deportation. U.S. citizens protesting this patently un-American spectacle have been killed. Two years ago, Trump was elected with unprecedentedly high levels of support from Latino voters. Today, look at the House results in the heavily Hispanic Rio Grande Valley of Texas: solid blue. It’s over. Trump might spend his remaining time in office doubling down on all of his transgressive and ruinous policies. He might retreat and focus on his building projects—his precious ballroom, his longed-for triumphal arch; indeed, he delivered the closing argument for his party at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, whose renovation he botched. Predictably, he blames the losing GOP candidates (including those he picked) for yesterday’s wipeout. But he no longer defines our time. A new era begins.

items.title: Le récit d’une nation à l’ambition universelle (par Pape Mahawa DIOUF)
items.description: Parmi les 54 comités olympiques nationaux du continent, le choix s’est porté sur le Sénégal pour organiser les premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse en Afrique. Le leadership de Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye y est assurément pour beaucoup. Mais pourquoi avoir fait confiance au Sénégal ? Durant quinze jours, 217 délégations et 2 700 jeunes athlètes âgés de 14 à 17 ans seront réunis à Dakar, Saly et Diamniadio pour célébrer le sport et l’esprit olympique. Il faut saluer le COJOJ pour son efficacité et la prouesse exemplaire qu’il est en train de réaliser. Cette réussite n’aurait toutefois pu voir le jour sans l’œuvre colossale du président Macky Sall : voies de communication, système de transport de masse moderne, intelligent et multimodal, infrastructures sportives de dernière génération. Ce sont ces équipements qui accueillent un événement de dimension mondiale. La ville de Dakar, sous le leadership de Khalifa Ababacar Sall puis de Soham El Wardini, a porté une candidature solide. Enfin, sans le leadership républicain du pésident Bassirou Diomaye Faye, les Jeux auraient été compromis par des atermoiements, des louvoiements et des puérilités politiciennes. C’est pourquoi nous nous réjouissons de voir un Sénégal qui rassemble ses meilleurs fils et filles pour servir son destin singulier de pays phare sur le continent africain. L’impact du soft power sénégalais À travers ces Jeux, il apparaît clairement que le génie sénégalais ne réside pas encore dans le « oil and gas » ; il tient toujours à la puissance de son soft power. Dakar, 1966 : le Sénégal accueille le monde, plus précisément le monde noir. C’est le Festival mondial des arts nègres (FESMAN). Qu’était donc le FESMAN ? Lancé sous l’impulsion de Léopold Sédar Senghor et d’Alioune Diop, avec la revue Présence africaine, le Festival fut un événement culturel grandiose conçu pour célébrer la culture, les arts, la littérature, le cinéma et l’identité des peuples d’Afrique et de sa diaspora — Haïti, États-Unis, Brésil, Caraïbes. André Malraux, ministre français de la Culture, mesurant parfaitement la portée du moment, déclara : « Nous voici donc dans l’histoire. Pour la première fois, un chef d’État prend en ses mains périssables le destin spirituel d’un continent. » Les petits-enfants de Senghor ont repris le flambeau. À travers ces Jeux, le peuple sénégalais rappelle ce qu’il est et poursuit sa trajectoire. Refuser le blocage institutionnel du Sénégal Il appartient donc au président Bassirou Diomaye Faye de consolider cette place que le monde nous reconnaît, ce phare que le continent regarde. Préserver notre démocratie de ses pourfendeurs : le blocage institutionnel que tentent les forces rétrogrades à l’Assemblée ne doit pas passer. Parce qu’elles divisent — jusque dans nos foyers —, détruisent ce que nous avons de plus cher — la paix et la concorde nationale — et chahutent nos institutions : aujourd’hui l’Assemblée nationale ; avant cela, la Justice et le président de la République. Je demeure convaincu qu’il faut les combattre par tous les moyens démocratiques et légaux. Face aux tentatives de détruire la réputation du Sénégal, tous les véritables patriotes doivent se dresser comme un seul homme et préserver ce legs précieux des pères fondateurs, que nous venons encore une fois de célébrer. S’il ne devait rester qu’une seule mission au président Bassirou Diomaye Faye, ce serait : redonner confiance, optimisme et fierté d’être ce que nous sommes: Sénégalais. Pape Mahawa DIOUF

items.title: Exploitation minière à Siguiri : entre impératif écologique, rigueur administrative et amalgames géopolitiques (Par Mamadou Oury Diallo)
items.description: L’actualité récente en Haute-Guinée, particulièrement dans la préfecture de Siguiri, alimente les conversations et suscite parfois des interprétations hâtives. Entre la décision d’interdire l’orpaillage artisanal, le limogeage de 479 responsables de districts et quartiers, et la radiation de 22 administrateurs territoriaux par le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, le pouvoir central a posé un acte d'une sévérité inédite. Parallèlement, le départ massif d'orpailleurs ressortissants du Burkina Faso vers Bamako a donné lieu à des narratifs complaisants, suggérant une vague d'expulsions ciblées ou xénophobes. Une analyse objective des faits impose de dissocier le bruit ambiant des réseaux sociaux de la réalité juridique, environnementale et administrative du dossier. Une décision ancrée dans la légalité et la souveraineté de l'État Sur le plan strictement juridique, l’action du gouvernement guinéen s’inscrit pleinement dans le cadre du Code minier et du Code de l'environnement de la République de Guinée. La régulation, voire la suspension temporaire ou définitive des activités minières artisanales lorsqu'elles menacent l'ordre public ou la salubrité publique, relève des prérogatives régaliennes fondamentales de tout État souverain. La légitimité de cette mesure repose sur un constat alarmant : la dégradation accélérée du bassin versant du fleuve Niger et des terres agricoles de la région de Siguiri. L’usage incontrôlé de produit s chimiques hautement toxiques, à commence r par le cyanure et le mercure, pour l’extraction et le traitement de l’or artisanal , constitue un danger sanitaire immédiat pour les populations riveraines et une catastrophe écologique irrémédiable pour les générations futures. L’exode des orpailleurs : un amalgame à déconstruire Pour l'observateur non averti, la coïncidence entre la décision d'interdiction et les mouvements de population transfrontaliers a pu prêter à confusion. Il est crucial de rétablir la vérité des faits : le départ des ressortissants burkinabè vers le Mali ou leur pays d'origine ne résulte nullement d'un arrêté d'expulsion visant une nationalité spécifique, mais bien des conséquences économiques mécaniques de l'arrêt des activités d'extraction. Cette problématique d'exploitation nocive dépasse d'ailleurs largement les frontières guinéennes. Pour preuve, le président de la transition burkinabè lui-même, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, dénonçait publiquement dans une récente intervention les ravages causés par certains de ses propres compatriotes utilisant du cyanure dans les sites d'orpaillage au Burkina Faso. Cette prise de parole du chef de l'État burkinabè illustre parfaitement qu'il ne s'agit en aucun cas d'un différend nationaliste ou d'une stigmatisation des citoyens d'un pays voisin, mais d'un combat continental et partagé contre un mode d'exploitation destructeur. Sanctionner la gouvernance locale : le signal de la responsabilité La sanction sans précédent infligée à l'appareil administratif local (22 administrateurs territoriaux radiés et 479 chefs de districts et quartiers démis de leurs fonctions) démontre que la réponse de l'État vise d'abord des défaillances internes. Ces mesures disciplinaires viennent réprimer la complicité, la tolérance passive ou le laissez-faire d’autorités locales ayant fermé les yeux sur des pratiques illégales et polluantes au détriment de l'intérêt général. En assainissant la chaîne de commandement territorial, le gouvernement entend rappeler une règle simple : la responsabilité de la protection de l'environnement et de la santé publique commence au cœur même des institutions de l'État. La décisio n des autorités à Siguiri ne saurait être réduite à une simple opération sécuritaire ou à un contentieux migratoire. Elle répond à un impératif de préservation de l'écosystème guinéen et de santé publique. En recadrant le débat autour de ses enjeux réels, la lutte contre la pollution au cyanure et la défaill ance des cadres administratifs , la Guinée rappelle que la souveraineté environnementale ne se négocie pas. Mamadou Oury DIALLO L’article Exploitation minière à Siguiri : entre impératif écologique, rigueur administrative et amalgames géopolitiques (Par Mamadou Oury Diallo) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Huile de table : le groupe La Belle rassure sur sa disponibilité
items.description: Le groupe agroalimentaire privé La Belle a publié ce mercredi 4 novembre un communiqué pour rassurer les Algériens sur la disponibilité de l’huile de table sur le marché national. « Le groupe La Belle tient à rassurer les citoyens : l'huile est bien disponible sur le marché. Ses unités de production continuent de fonctionner à un rythme régulier et à pleine capacité, afin de répondre aux besoins du marché national et de garantir des quantités suffisantes pour couvrir les besoins des consommateurs à travers tout le pays », a-t-il indiqué dans un communiqué publié sur les réseaux sociaux. Ce message survient alors que des rumeurs commencent à se propager sur d’éventuelles tensions sur l’huile végétale sur le marché national. Le groupe La Belle anticipe ces tensions dans le but d'éviter des achats massifs de la part des citoyens, ce qui pourrait provoquer des tensions sur ce produit de large consommation et qui bénéficie de la subvention de l’État. Huile de table : le groupe La Belle s’engage à approvisionner le marché de manière continue Dans son communiqué, le groupe La Belle a réaffirmé son « engagement à poursuivre la production et l'approvisionnement de manière continue, contribuant ainsi à maintenir la stabilité du marché et à assurer la disponibilité constante de ce produit de première nécessité ». L’Algérie produit plus d’un million de tonnes d’huile végétale par an. Les prix de ce produit de grande consommation, qui est très prisé par les ménages et les fast-foods, sont plafonnés par l’État : 125 dinars pour la bouteille d’un litre, 250 DA pour celle de 2 litres et 650 dinars pour celle de 5 litres. L’article Huile de table : le groupe La Belle rassure sur sa disponibilité est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2Baba ends six-year album wait, announces ‘Oldest Young Man’ release date
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has announced November 27, 2026, as the release date for his forthcoming album, ‘Oldest Young Man’, his first studio project in six years. The singer announced the date in a post on his Instagram handle on Tuesday, describing the project as timeless music. “The legacy continues. OLDEST YOUNG MAN drops 27.11.26. Timeless music, no expiration date,” he wrote. View this post on Instagram The announcement comes after months of teasing the album on social media, with 2Baba repeatedly using its title in his Instagram captions. In August, he wrote: “I’ve lived it, I’ve seen it, I’m still here. My new album, Oldest Young Man, soon come.” On his birthday, the singer also described himself as the “forever the oldest young man”. The upcoming project will be his first album since ‘Warriors’, released in 2020, which was his eighth studio album. 2Baba first rose to prominence in the 1990s, composing jingles before co-founding the music group Plantashun Boiz with Blackface and Faze in 1996. He later established himself as one of the pioneers of Afropop, influencing generations of Nigerian artistes with his music. His album releases include ‘Face 2 Face’ (2004), ‘Grass 2 Grace’ (2006), ‘The Unstoppable’ (2009), ‘The Unstoppable International Edition’ (2010), ‘Away and Beyond’ (2012), ‘The Ascension’, ‘Rewind, Select, Update’ (2015) and ‘Warriors’ (2020). Vanguard News The post 2Baba ends six-year album wait, announces ‘Oldest Young Man’ release date appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Singer Tofamba confronts fear, embraces self-discovery in new single ‘AsumDwe’
items.description: Ghanaian singer Tofamba is set to release a new single, AsumDwe, on November 6, drawing on personal experiences to explore themes of inner peace, self-discovery, freedom and personal growth. The song reflects her journey towards confronting fear, overcoming personal limitations and embracing life’s challenges. Tofamba says the inspiration came from realising that avoiding difficult situations does not make them disappear. “I realised that I couldn’t keep running from the things holding me back. I had to face them,” she said. Although rooted in her personal experiences, the singer hopes the song will connect with listeners navigating their own struggles and remind them that they are not alone. She describes life as the biggest influence on the record, explaining that its message draws directly from experiences she has encountered. “Nothing teaches you better than life itself. Everything you hear in ‘AsumDwe’ comes from experiences life has handed me,” she said. She further summed up her creative inspiration with the remark: “Life overfed me, so I had to spit it out.” The production process also involved making difficult creative choices, with the team eventually removing some elements to preserve the song’s original direction. “Sometimes, knowing what to leave out is just as important as knowing what to put in,” she noted. Beyond its themes, AsumDwe represents a stage in Tofamba’s personal and artistic development. Asked whether the song reflects the woman she is today or the person she is becoming, she described it as “more of a glimpse of the woman I am becoming.” Her outlook is captured in the Ghanaian expression, “Daakye Bɛyɛ Dɛ”, meaning tomorrow will be beautiful. Through the song, Tofamba hopes to encourage courage, self-belief and the determination to keep moving forward despite life’s difficulties. She believes that present circumstances should not define people’s potential and that fear should not prevent them from pursuing the people they aspire to become. AsumDwe is scheduled for release on November 6.

items.title: I had a great experience at Pope John Senior High School – MC Kabutey reveals
items.description: Ghanaian MC Alfred Kabutey Ocansey, popularly known as ‘MC Kabutey’, has shared fond memories of his time at Pope John Senior High School, describing his boarding school experience as one filled with unforgettable moments, friendships and lessons. Speaking on The Career Trail Season 4 on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, he recalled how his interest in hockey began at the school, partly because of his mother’s own experience with the sport. According to him, hockey was a big deal at Pope John at the time and was even featured on the school’s official prospectus. His mother, who had played the sport at university, was excited when she saw it and made sure he got his own hockey stick. “I remember we went to town to get a hockey stick. We got a Slazenger fiberglass coated hockey stick,” he recounted. The stick soon became his ticket into the school hockey team, as some seniors wanted to use it and had to persuade him to join before they could get access to it. “The seniors wanted to use my stick, so they had to convince me to join the hockey team,” he revealed. But beyond hockey, MC Kabutey recalled the unusual circumstances surrounding his year group’s accommodation when they arrived at the school in 1997. With their assigned house full, some of the first-year students were moved into a room above the administration block, where about 12 to 16 of them shared space with two senior students. The arrangement earned them the nickname “Administration Top Boys”. They always had food, making them a convenient stop for seniors whenever they were hungry. “If seniors are hungry, they will come to us. Because they know that those boys there are sorted,” he explained. Despite the good memories, MC Kabutey admitted that his time at Pope John was not without its difficult moments, particularly the bullying he experienced from senior students. He explained that his year group was among the first batches from the JHS system to encounter the final groups of O-Level and A-Level students, who were much older and physically stronger. “The O-Level and A-Level guys… Me, when I was going to secondary school, I didn’t have a beard. I had not even seen somebody with a full beard in my house. These guys, they have proper beards. Because they were literally like uncles. You know what I mean? Grown guys, strong guys, solid guys,” he highlighted. “From the first day at the bathhouse, lining you up and doing ‘sizing’ and all kinds of things, from room to room, to taking our food, and sending us on weeding escapades. I mean, all of that was part of the experience,” he continued. Although the experience came with its fair share of challenges, MC Kabutey said his years at Pope John remained memorable. He recalled recently reuniting with one of his former seniors, Raymond, at an international conference in Accra, where he was the event host. The two shared a laugh as he reminded Raymond of how much he had bullied him during their school days. MC Kabutey finally paid tribute to his former schoolmates, particularly the 1999 year group, popularly known as the Pojoba year group.

Le diplomate algérien était porteur d’un message écrit de Son Excellence Monsieur Abdelmadjid TEBBOUNE, Président de la République Algérienne Démocratique et Populaire, à son frère le Président ABDOURAHAMANE TIANI. À l’issue de l’audience, le Ministre d’État algérien a indiqué que les échanges ont porté sur le renforcement de la coopération bilatérale qui, depuis la visite d’État de Son Excellence, le Général d’Armée, ABDOURAHAMANE TIANI à Alger, connaît une dynamique sans précédent, au bénéfice des deux peuples frères. Les deux parties ont également évoqué la situation sécuritaire au Sahel et réaffirmé leur volonté commune d’œuvrer pour la stabilité et le développement de l’espace sahélien, en transformant les foyers de crise en foyers de paix et de prospérité. items.title: El Rey inaugura la XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana alabando que la comunidad de naciones “franquea el acceso a un espacio de mayor libertad y prosperidad”
items.description: La XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana de Madrid ha quedado oficialmente inaugurada este miércoles con un espectáculo al atardecer en el Teatro Real, que ha contado con las actuaciones de algunas de las figuras más reconocidas del espacio iberoamericano, y con una colección de discursos de carga política por parte de las autoridades: “Creo que nuestra identidad compartida —entre el pasado y el futuro, entre la memoria y la aspiración— es una brújula indispensable para navegar este convulso el siglo XXI”, ha esbozado el rey Felipe VI en su alocución inaugural de un foro con el que España, como país anfitrión, aspira a reflotar los lazos entre Estados iberoamericanos. Seguir leyendo El Rey ensalza el “ingente trabajo” de la cumbre Iberoamericana para llegar a acuerdos Felipe VI y Letizia Ortiz ofrecieron anoche una cena a los mandatarios que hoy intervienen en el plenario de la XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana, que este año ha tenido como escenario el centro de Madrid. En su brindis inicial, el Rey hizo alusión a la importancia de esta cumbre y al “ingente trabajo” preparatorio que conlleva para que, al final, los diferentes países que componen esta comunidad lleguen a acuerdos. Lo ha dicho justo en una edición que resulta un poco descafeinada con la ausencia de mandatarios de países clave como México, Brasil o Venezuela. Sí asiste el polémico Javier Milei, presidente de Argentina, que, sin embargo, se ausentó anoche de la ceremonia de inauguración en el Teatro Real y la posterior cena en el Palacio por motivos de agenda. Se da la circunstancia de que Milei, en las ocho veces que ha viajado a España, no se ha reunido nunca ni con Felipe VI ni con Pedro Sánchez. Se prevé que hoy sea su primer encuentro. En su discurso, en el que subraya la importancia de estas reuniones, Felipe VI ha remarcado que el objetivo es mejorar la vida de los más de 700 millones de personas que componen la comunidad Iberoamericana. La cotidianidad, ha dicho. “La agenda la marcan, casi siempre, asuntos centrales en la vida cotidiana. Y así debe ser. Acercarse a lo que ocupa y preocupa a la ciudadanía —es decir, serles útil— ha de ser la prioridad de la Comunidad Iberoamericana de Naciones: la mejora de las condiciones de vida como razón primera y última de nuestra cooperación, siempre con el reconocimiento de la dignidad de todo ser humano como faro que guie nuestra acción”, ha dicho el monarca. Como temas encima de la mesa, Felipe VI ha marcado cuatro prioridades: uno, coordinación ante desastres naturales; dos, el reconocimiento de títulos académicos; tres, el tratamiento de los datos personales en el mundo digital; y cuatro, la consideración del cuidado como derecho y bien público esencial.

items.title: Cargill Kokoo Sourcing Limited rewards 563 cocoa farmers with pruning machines as it marks 10 years
items.description: Cargill Kokoo Sourcing Limited has rewarded 563 cocoa farmers with standard pruning machines as part of activities marking 10 years of cocoa sourcing operations in Ghana. The gesture forms part of the company’s efforts to recognise farmers’ contributions to the cocoa industry and support their farming activities. The anniversary celebrations, held from October 28 to 30, 2026, took place across the 21 districts where the company has operated since its establishment in 2016. The celebrations brought together cocoa farmers, traditional authorities, buyer agents, community representatives and other stakeholders to reflect on the company’s decade-long operations and recognise the partnerships that have supported its growth. In addition to the pruning machines, more than 2,000 farmers received company souvenirs in appreciation of their contributions to its operations. Cargill Kokoo Sourcing said cocoa farmers remain central to its business, noting that their hard work, resilience and dedication sustain Ghana’s cocoa industry, support rural livelihoods and connect farming communities to global markets. The company also highlighted its contribution to youth employment, revealing that it had created opportunities for more than 700 young graduates who have worked as buyer agents over the past decade. According to the company, the graduates have gained practical work experience and professional skills while supporting cocoa sourcing activities and building relationships with farmers across its operational districts. Since commencing operations in 2016, Cargill Kokoo Sourcing has worked with farmers, buyer agents, traditional authorities and local communities to strengthen its sourcing network and promote responsible cocoa production. As it looks to the next decade, the company says it remains committed to sustainable sourcing practices, stronger partnerships and creating opportunities for young professionals in Ghana’s cocoa sector. Cargill has been sourcing cocoa from Ghana for more than 40 years. In 2008, it established a cocoa processing facility in Tema, before adding a licensed buying company to its Ghanaian operations in 2016.

VAST Ghana, SEND Ghana, and GAND join forces to reshape Ghana’s food environment
items.description: VAST Ghana, SEND Ghana and the Ghana Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics (GAND) have joined forces to advocate stronger policies to promote healthy eating and tackle the growing burden of diet-related diseases in Ghana. The public health advocacy groups made the call at a workshop on Nutrient Profile Modelling (NPM), Front-of-Pack Warning Labelling (FOPWL) and healthy food policies, where they highlighted the need for measures that will help consumers make informed food choices and improve the country’s food environment. The workshop brought together perspectives from nutrition experts and civil society advocates on the growing availability and promotion of processed foods, many of which contain high levels of sugar, salt and unhealthy fats. President of GAND, Rev. Prince Baidoo, said Ghana’s food environment had changed significantly over the past decade, with processed and imported foods becoming increasingly available and influencing people’s eating habits. He said the country had a wide range of nutritious indigenous foods, but the growing consumption of processed products was exposing people to excessive amounts of sugar, salt and unhealthy fats. “For the past few years, maybe over a decade now, we’ve had a lot of changes in our diet because most of our foods are now being processed, and some are being imported. So, we have a mixed food environment now,” he said. Rev. Baidoo explained that manufacturers often add sugar, salt and fat to processed foods to make them more appealing to consumers. He warned that the amount of sugar in some products could be much higher than consumers realise. “Normally, if somebody is taking ‘koko’, you just take your cup of cocoa and add a cube of sugar or two to it. Now, that cube of sugar or two, when translated to how manufactured products are, they will come in like six, nine, 10 cubes of sugar and you wouldn’t even know because it’s embedded in the manufacturing,” he said. He said excessive consumption of sugar, salt and unhealthy fats could contribute to diabetes, hypertension, weight gain, high cholesterol, heart disease and stroke, while also increasing the risk of some cancers. According to him, high sugar consumption can affect insulin levels and the body’s ability to regulate blood sugar, while excessive salt intake can increase blood pressure. He also warned that trans fats in some pastries and processed foods could raise cholesterol levels and contribute to the blockage of arteries. Rev. Baidoo expressed particular concern about the increasing number of children developing conditions traditionally associated with adults. “This is one of the heart-aching moments for us as nutrition and dietetic advocates in Ghana. We are having a lot of our children having diseases that we designate as adult diseases,” he said. He attributed the trend partly to children’s increasing consumption of sugary drinks, pastries and processed meat products such as sausages, which he said can contain high levels of salt and fat. He said that children were increasingly exposed to unhealthy eating habits at an early age, rather than developing such habits gradually as they grew older. Rev. Baidoo said childhood obesity was also increasing, pointing to trends in demographic and health survey reports over the years. He called for a return to healthier indigenous meals, including beans, banku and okro, kenkey with fish and pepper, and fufu with light soup. “Ghana, we are not bereft of healthy meals. Our meals are beans, banku and okro, kenkey, fish and pepper, and we can have our fufu and light soup. These are foods that our ancestors had. Let’s get our people to be eating our indigenous diet,” he said. He added that exotic and manufactured foods could be consumed occasionally, particularly at parties and other special events, rather than becoming a regular part of people’s diets. Executive Director of VAST Ghana, Labram Musah, raised concerns about the influence of the food industry on public health policies, warning that commercial interests could undermine efforts to reduce the consumption of unhealthy products. He explained that the food industry involved a wide range of actors, from agricultural producers and manufacturers to packaging companies, retailers, supermarkets, advertising firms and lobby groups. Mr Musah said industry interference referred to tactics used by companies to block, delay, weaken or undermine public health policies aimed at reducing the consumption of unhealthy products. He argued that the profit-driven nature of the industry could create a conflict between commercial interests and public health objectives. “Industry interference refers to the range of tactics and activities used by industry companies to block, delay, weaken or undermine public health policies aimed at reducing the use or consumption of unhealthy food products,” he said. According to him, some companies use sponsorships, corporate social responsibility programmes, lobbying and other forms of engagement to influence policy discussions and build relationships with decision-makers. He also identified what he described as the industry’s four Ds: delay, divide, deflect and deny. Mr Musah said companies could delay the introduction of policies, create divisions among public health advocates, shift attention away from the health effects of their products, and challenge evidence of the harm associated with their consumption. He cited arguments around the economic impact of proposed regulations, including claims that taxes on alcoholic beverages could lead to the loss of 2,000 jobs. He said civil society advocates had challenged the figure and called on the industry to provide justification for the claim. Mr Musah also criticised efforts to shift responsibility for unhealthy consumption entirely to individuals, arguing that government had a duty to protect public health through effective regulation. He called for a clear distinction between commercial interests and public health policymaking to prevent industry influence from weakening interventions intended to protect consumers. He further urged the government to reconsider changes to the tax on sweetened beverages, calling for the reinstatement of a 13 per cent levy. Mr Musah said that claims about the health benefits of some products should not be used to justify reduced taxation, particularly where those products still contain added sugar. He also called for a clear definition of fruit juice to prevent manufacturers from using vague descriptions to influence how consumers understand their products. Project Officer at SEND Ghana, Baaba Sam, said Ghana already had food labelling requirements that provided nutritional information on the back of packaged products, but the system was not compulsory and was often poorly understood by consumers. She said the information could help consumers identify the amount of sugar, fat and salt in food products, but many people either ignored it or struggled to interpret the figures. “Ghana has a regulation for food labelling, actually. So, when you take any product, and then you look at the back of the label, you see that there’s a nutrition content table over there,” she said. “But the issue with it is that it’s actually not compulsory, so people cannot decide whether or not they want to put it there. The other part is that consumers do not understand. So, the ordinary Ghanaian does not understand, and we don’t even pay attention to it at all,” she added. Ms Sam said mandatory Front-of-Pack Warning Labelling would make nutritional information more accessible and easier to understand. She explained that the proposed labels would include symbols and written warnings to help consumers identify products containing excessive amounts of unhealthy nutrients. “The front-of-pack warning policy, or the FOPL, has two sides. One, it would have a symbol, and it would also have writing so that if the person, the consumer, is not educated, at least when you see the symbol, it gives you an idea of what the label is trying to warn you about,” she said. She also raised concerns about the use of very small print on some food packages, saying it made nutritional information difficult to read. “That is why the front-of-pack labelling policy is coming again to make it bold, legible, easy to read and understand, because if it is small, then why is it there in the first place if people cannot read it?” she asked. Ms Sam further urged parents to make healthier food choices for their children, warning that packaged snacks were often prioritised over fruits and vegetables because they were convenient and easily accessible. “Parents, when we are deciding the kind of snacks to give our children, fruits don’t come to mind, or vegetables don’t come to mind, but the first thing we go for actually, parents buy it in packs, and they put it down because it’s easy, it’s accessible and all that,” she said. “Forgetting that we are raising future diabetics and future hypertensives,” she warned. She said the increasing diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes among children showed the need for urgent action to improve eating habits and protect the health of future generations. Ms Sam also warned that the growing burden of chronic diseases could place additional pressure on government spending, as more resources would be required to manage conditions that often need long-term treatment. “The health of its people is what drives the economy. And so, if you now have to spend a lot of money, like the government is doing now, to take care of your population, it’s a chronic disease that is not going. And so, it’s like just managing the person to live,” she said.

items.title: Trump Learns His Orbán Lesson
items.description: The president of the world’s greatest democracy admires autocratic leaders. He speaks with great affection about Russia’s Vladimir Putin, China’s Xi Jinping, and even North Korea’s Kim Jong Un. But the model that he and his MAGA acolytes have long apparently hoped to emulate was that of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who ruled for some 20 years by boring into Hungary’s democratic institutions, including the media and the courts, and either gutting or corrupting them. Trump tried his best, and it has now led him to the same dead end. Last spring, Hungary experienced the highest voter turnout since the country’s 1990 transition to democracy. Voters threw out Orbán and his party, Fidesz, in favor of a former Fidesz member, Peter Magyar, who’d tied Orbán to autocracy, corruption, and decreasing living standards. Orbán, who was widely expected to do whatever he could to subvert the vote, realized he faced a result too big to challenge. The numbers were overwhelming in every corner of Hungary, and Orbán could not remotely make even a laughable case for casting doubt on the result. Last night, Trump and his party experienced a similar fate as they suffered the consequences of their brazen attacks on American democracy, of allowing the stench of corruption to envelop the White House, of starting a foolish and unpopular war, and of promising a better economy and instead delivering inflation and high gas prices. Like Orbán, he had to sit helplessly and watch his party take beatings from the Democratic Party in places where Democrats were supposedly almost extinct. (In Kansas, the Democrat Adam Hamilton will become a senator. Hamilton was born in 1964. The last Democratic senator from Kansas was born in 1879 .) [ Read: Trump repeats a centuries-old mistake ] The president’s reaction to this crushing loss has been remarkably muted. As vote counting began, Trump spent his time excoriating not the Democrats but, for some reason, Fox News. On Truth Social , he railed about how much he hated the voice of one of Fox’s few in-house liberal commentators, Jessica Tarlov, and claimed that Fox’s ratings were down “because they’re spending too much time covering the Trump Deranged Dumocrats.” In fact, Trump said, Fox was ignoring a CNN poll that showed him to be more popular among Republicans than Abraham Lincoln. (In reality, the poll asked an open-ended question about which president people most admire, and the respondents tended to choose recent presidents.) As the night wore on and Republican losses piled up, Trump, who often posts barrages of messages, was unusually quiet. Shortly after 10:30 p.m. eastern time, he reacted to the accelerating bad news by donning the suit of armor made of his high-tensile-strength narcissism. “I wasn’t on the Ballot,” he whined, “and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” (And then, of course: “Thank you for your attention to this matter.”) The problem is that Trump, over the past weeks, challenged Americans to vote as if he were on the ballot, and millions of people apparently took him up on the offer. By late evening, Trump’s transformation into Orbán was complete. He said —again without his characteristic combativeness—that he would accept the outcome of the election and that he would be willing to work with Democrats. Whether he means to hold to those commitments is anyone’s guess. (At the same time he was sounding conciliatory, he posted a picture of a hat with the word VETO on it.) This morning, Trump appeared at the worksite of his beloved White House ballroom. When reporters asked him about the election, he quietly deflected, saying that he would not have done anything differently, and then went back to talking about marble and kitchens. [ Read: The simple message that produced a Democratic landslide ] Whether Trump has sincerely accepted the victory of the Democrats and intends to cooperate with them in governing the country is, in a sense, irrelevant: The more important reality is that he faces an electoral result too decisive to challenge, as Orbán did. I was among the many who feared that he might inundate state election authorities with lawsuits or even try to seize ballots, but those possibilities evaporated before midnight. So many votes had been cast, even in red states, that any attempt to undermine the result would look either violently dictatorial or patently ridiculous. Trump, like Orbán, wanted to seize power using democratic means, and then eviscerate any future challenges to his power by destroying those same practices and institutions. Like Orbán, Trump’s arrogance, contempt for the law and toleration of corruption, and staggering incompetence pushed even former supporters beyond their limits. Unlike Orbán, he does not have to leave office, and he could provoke any number of crises between now and the 2028 elections. But he seems genuinely deflated by the scale of punishment that the American people have inflicted on his party and his chosen candidates. The Hungarians, many of whom perhaps thought Orbán was destined to be a permanent fixture in their life, relearned the lesson of their Cold War liberation: Mobilization, organization, and voting can bring down an autocracy. Last night, Americans proved that the same methods can forestall one.

items.title: Liverpool collapse to Champions League defeat at Fenerbahce
items.description: Dirk Kuyt got the better of his former club Liverpool as Fenerbahce twice came from behind for a famous 3-2 win in Istanbul that breathed new life into their Champions League campaign. Liverpool had won their opening three European games under Andoni Iraola, but were punished for sloppy defending in a surprise defeat. Trey Nyoni and substitute Alexander Isak twice put the visitors in front. But Liverpool, who lost twice away to Galatasaray last season, were beaten again in Istanbul as Englishmen Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown levelled before Vedat Muriqi’s winner. Fenerbahce’s interim boss Kuyt, who spent six years at Anfield as a player, was taking charge for just the second time after Ismail Kartal quit last week. The Turkish giants had taken just two points from their opening three Champions League games but made the most of Liverpool’s generosity at the back. Liverpool’s perfect Champions League start allowed Iraola the luxury of leaving out Isak and Florian Wirtz among five changes from Sunday’s 1-0 defeat by Arsenal. Nyoni retained his place and capped another fine performance with his first Liverpool goal from the edge of the box. Just four minutes later, though, Alisson Becker was deceived by Greenwood’s deflected free-kick to equalise. Iraola unleashed Isak, Wirtz and Cody Gakpo from the bench just after the hour mark and got an almost immediate reward. Isak was afforded far too much space to head in Gakpo’s cross. But again Liverpool quickly handed back their advantage. Gakpo’s touch inadvertently deflected a cross beyond Alisson to give Brown an easy tap-in at the back post. Liverpool then conceded for the 10th time in four Champions League games when Muriqi outmuscled Jeremy Jacquet to a looping cross and steered a header into the bottom corner. Defeat cost Liverpool the chance to move level with Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table as they sit. Victory moves Fenerbahce move up to 19th in the 36-team table. items.title: Breaking: Flamingos beat Brazil to reach first U17 Women World Cup final
items.description: Nigeria’s U17 women’s team, the Flamingos, have reached the final of the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup for the first time in history after defeating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final. The Flamingos secured the historic victory with goals from Queen Joseph and Awawu Bashiru, who scored twice. Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute before Bashiru extended Nigeria’s lead in the 71st minute. Bashiru completed her brace in the 80th minute to seal Nigeria’s 3-1 victory and book their place in the final. The achievement marks a major milestone for the Nigerian side, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition. The Flamingos will now face Japan in the final as they seek to win their first-ever FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup title. items.title: Ouahbi : 8 millions de dossiers judiciaires répertoriés en trois ans
items.description: Le ministère de la Justice entend accélérer la numérisation des archives judiciaires marocaines. Sur les quelque 160 millions de dossiers conservés dans les tribunaux, près de 8 millions ont été répertoriés au cours des trois dernières années, a annoncé, mercredi 4 novembre, le ministre de la Justice, Abdellatif Ouahbi. L’objectif est de faciliter l’accès aux documents grâce à une plateforme électronique permettant de localiser précisément leur lieu de conservation. Présentant le projet de budget sectoriel de son département pour l’exercice 2027 devant la commission de la justice, de la législation, des droits de l’homme et des libertés à la Chambre des représentants, le ministre a détaillé les contours de cette initiative. Le chantier prévoit l’organisation des archives judiciaires, la numérisation des dossiers et l’identification des parties concernées. Il doit permettre aux justiciables de retrouver leurs documents et de connaître leur emplacement dans les dépôts, sans démarches administratives complexes ni recherches fastidieuses. Des archives particulièrement sensibles Pour Abdellatif Ouahbi, la gestion des archives constitue l’un des dossiers les plus sensibles auxquels son ministère doit faire face. Ces documents touchent directement à la vie des citoyens, à leurs secrets, à leurs biens, à leur honneur, à leur filiation et à leurs héritages. Or, les conditions actuelles de conservation soulèvent des difficultés : certains dossiers sont entreposés dans des dépôts, tandis que d’autres se trouvent dans les sous-sols des tribunaux. Leur protection et leur organisation apparaissent dès lors comme une nécessité urgente. Le périmètre du projet devrait également être élargi aux archives des notaires décédés ou ayant cessé d’exercer. Ces documents renferment des informations essentielles sur les biens des citoyens, leurs testaments et leurs droits. Une numérisation globale pour éviter les doublons Le ministre est également revenu sur les difficultés ayant accompagné le processus de numérisation des tribunaux. Il a expliqué que le ministère de la Justice et l’autorité judiciaire avaient, à certaines étapes, développé séparément leurs propres programmes numériques. Cette organisation a conduit à mobiliser des crédits pour des logiciels similaires, voire redondants, alors qu’ils concernaient le même service public. © Mounir Mehimdate Pour remédier à cette situation, les deux institutions ont engagé des discussions afin de mettre fin aux doublons et de s’accorder sur une numérisation globale du système judiciaire. Le budget du projet a été convenu avec le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances. Les échanges ont également porté sur la désignation de l’entité chargée de l’exécution des dépenses et du règlement des prestations dues aux institutions responsables de sa mise en œuvre. La sensibilité des données judiciaires a toutefois soulevé une question supplémentaire : celle du recours au secteur privé. Les informations concernées comprennent notamment les noms des accusés et des témoins, ainsi que des éléments confidentiels contenus dans les dossiers. Le ministère s’est finalement orienté vers l’attribution du projet à une institution publique. Ouahbi a, dans ce cadre, proposé de confier la qualité d’ordonnateur au président délégué du Conseil supérieur du pouvoir judiciaire, afin d’éviter les complications liées aux procédures de dépense des crédits au sein du ministère. Clarifier les compétences pour préserver l’indépendance judiciaire Au-delà de la transformation numérique, le ministre a insisté sur la nécessité de clarifier les relations entre son département et le pouvoir judiciaire. Il a défendu l’indépendance de l’autorité judiciaire et du parquet à l’égard du ministère, tout en soulignant l’importance de la coopération et de la coordination entre les institutions. Une délimitation insuffisamment claire des compétences, a-t-il averti, risque d’entraîner des chevauchements de prérogatives et de perturber le fonctionnement de la justice. Cette séparation implique notamment que le ministère ne puisse intervenir dans la gestion des affaires relatives aux magistrats ni consulter les rapports d’inspection les concernant. Ces documents peuvent contenir des informations confidentielles sur les dossiers et les délibérations. L’inspection de l’administration judiciaire et des fonctionnaires qui y travaillent relève, en revanche, des compétences du ministère. Pour mieux articuler les missions des deux institutions, une coordination entre leurs services d’inspection a été mise en place. Les inspecteurs du pouvoir judiciaire et ceux de l’administration judiciaire se rendent ainsi dans les tribunaux au cours de la même période, tout en conservant leur indépendance respective. Ce dispositif doit permettre de déterminer les responsabilités en cas de dysfonctionnement au sein des institutions judiciaires. La séparation des compétences s’est également accompagnée d’une distinction entre les budgets et les administrations relevant du pouvoir judiciaire et ceux du ministère de la Justice. Chaque institution dispose de son propre budget, dont la gestion doit respecter l’autonomie de ses prérogatives. Le ministre a illustré cette logique par la question des véhicules destinés aux responsables judiciaires. Selon lui, la remise directe d’une voiture par un ministre à un président de tribunal pourrait soulever des interrogations quant à l’indépendance de ce dernier. La procédure fait donc l’objet d’une coordination avec le président délégué du Conseil supérieur du pouvoir judiciaire, chargé de gérer cette opération. © Mounir Mehimdate La création d’un tribunal ne suffit pas à le faire fonctionner L’organisation des juridictions constitue un autre exemple de cette répartition des responsabilités. Ouahbi a rappelé que la création d’un tribunal par décret ne signifie pas nécessairement son ouverture immédiate. Son fonctionnement effectif dépend des nominations des responsables judiciaires, du président de la juridiction aux responsables du parquet, des compétences qui relèvent de l’autorité judiciaire. L’expérience a ainsi montré, selon lui, l’importance d’une concertation entre les deux institutions. Le ministère de la Justice assure la création des tribunaux et la mise en place des conditions nécessaires à leur fonctionnement, tandis que le pouvoir judiciaire procède aux nominations. Cette complémentarité doit permettre aux nouvelles juridictions d’entrer en activité sans entraves. Enfin, le ministre a souligné que les réformes législatives, administratives et judiciaires nécessitaient du temps avant de produire leurs effets. Leur mise en œuvre doit être suivie d’une évaluation des choix opérés et, si nécessaire, de corrections lorsque des dysfonctionnements sont constatés. « Le travail au sein du ministère, comme dans les autres secteurs gouvernementaux, demeure un travail humain susceptible d’erreurs et de corrections », a-t-il rappelé, insistant sur la nécessité d’inscrire les réformes dans une démarche d’amélioration continue. The post Ouahbi : 8 millions de dossiers judiciaires répertoriés en trois ans appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Dernier rappel pour le paiement de la taxe additionnelle sur les terrains non ou insuffisamment mis en valeur
items.description: ​La Direction générale des impôts (DGI) a rappelé, dans un communiqué en date du 3 novembre 2026, que la date limite pour le paiement de la taxe additionnelle applicable aux terrains non mis en valeur ou insuffisamment mis en valeur est fixée au 14 novembre 2026. ​Une échéance cruciale pour la première phase ​Cette première phase d'imposition concerne spécifiquement les parcelles aménagées par la Société nationale d'aménagement des terrains urbains (SONATUR) dans la région du Kadiogo, en particulier dans la zone de Ouaga 2000. Ces situations ont été établies à la suite des opérations de constat de mise en valeur engagées depuis juillet 2024. ​Conformément aux dispositions de l'article 279-8 du Code général des impôts, les contribuables concernés avaient déjà été informés des modalités de notification et des délais impartis via le communiqué n°2026-007/MEF/SG/DGI du 13 août 2026. ​Risque de retrait des parcelles ​Face à cette échéance imminente, la Directrice générale des impôts invite instamment les contribuables qui ne se sont pas encore acquittés de cette obligation fiscale à régulariser leur situation au plus tard le 14 novembre 2026. ​La DGI rappelle avec fermeté que le non-paiement de la taxe dans les délais prescrits expose les titulaires de droits concernés au retrait de leurs parcelles, conformément à la réglementation en vigueur. ​Où s'informer et payer ? ​Pour toute vérification ou information complémentaire relative aux parcelles concernées, les usagers peuvent se rendre, les jours ouvrables de 8h00 à 15h00, auprès des services fiscaux compétents selon la situation géographique de leur terrain : ​La Direction du centre des impôts Ouaga VI (DCI Ouaga VI) ; ​La Direction du centre des impôts Ouaga VIII (DCI Ouaga VIII) ; ​Le Centre départemental des impôts de Komsilga (CDI Komsilga). ​Par ailleurs, le montant de la taxe due pour chaque parcelle peut être consulté en ligne sur la plateforme dédiée : https://etitre2.dgi.bf. Des numéros utiles sont également mis à la disposition des contribuables : 58 87 17 26 / 78 50 81 80. items.title: ‘Hardest days of my life,’ Goalkeeper Owono speaks after Tenerife striker’s death
items.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said Wednesday he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, whom he collided with during a Spanish second division match on Monday. The 30-year-old Spanish footballer died Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in the sickening collision with Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who had raced into midfield to clear an aerial ball. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.” Spanish police sources told AFP an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision. Andorra players observed a minute’s silence on Wednesday before a voluntary training session, which Owono, 25, did not attend. Owono received support from the president of the African country’s federation, Venancio Tomas Micha, in a letter of condolence following De Miguel’s death. “I feel compelled to convey all our solidarity and support at this time to our player Jesus Lazaro Owono,” Tomas Micha wrote. “We know that, as the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress. “From the Equatorial Guinea Football Federation, we offer him all our human and professional backing, fully aware of the harshness of this event, which no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.” Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz posted on Instagram in support of Owono, whom he said was “deeply affected” by what had happened. “Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone,” wrote Spatz. “In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences.” – Postponements – Earlier it was confirmed Tenerife and Andorra’s Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend would be postponed. Tenerife were due to face Granada away from home, while Andorra were set to welcome Mallorca. “After the tragic news of the death of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, the game… this Saturday November 7, at Nuevo Los Carmenes (stadium), has been postponed,” said Granada in a statement. Mallorca said “at times like this, respect and sensitivity in the face of a situation of profound grief must come first”. The Spanish football federation postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches this week as a mark of respect following De Miguel’s death. Tenerife plan to hold a tribute to De Miguel at the club’s stadium on Saturday which supporters can attend, and are holding a six-day mourning period. The club said the first team, board and staff will attend De Miguel’s funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo on the Spanish mainland, where he has family roots. A minute of silence was held before Champions League matches on Tuesday in honour of the striker, with the same planned for the rest of the week’s fixtures organised by European football governing body UEFA. rbs/mw The post ‘Hardest days of my life,’ Goalkeeper Owono speaks after Tenerife striker’s death appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cocaine bust: NDC dismisses NPP calls for dismissal of Interior Minister, NACOC officials
items.description: The Deputy Director of Elections and IT of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Tanko Rashid-Computer, has dismissed calls by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) for the removal of the Interior Minister and officials of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) and Customs Division over alleged lapses in the fight against drug trafficking. He described the NPP’s allegations as baseless, accusing the opposition party of making claims that could later be withdrawn or explained away as metaphors. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story , Mr Rashid-Computer questioned the credibility of the NPP’s recent allegations, citing previous claims by some of its members that were subsequently described as metaphors by the Minority Leader, Alexander Afenyo-Markin. He recalled an earlier press conference at which a Vice Chairperson of the NPP allegedly claimed that a location in Accra was being used for cocaine production. According to him, Mr Afenyo-Markin later described the statement as a metaphor, arguing that the opposition should not expect the government to take its latest allegations seriously. “Dismiss them with the contempt they deserve,” he said when asked whether the NDC government would heed the NPP’s call for the removal of some government appointees. Mr Rashid-Computer, however, insisted that the government remained committed to tackling drug trafficking and would pursue everyone involved in the trade, including those who facilitate and benefit from the criminal activities. He cited a recent operation involving NACOC and Lebanese authorities, explaining that international drug trafficking networks required detailed investigations to identify all individuals involved in the supply chain. He said arresting only those physically transporting the drugs would not be enough to dismantle the networks, stressing the need to trace the organisers, collaborators and financiers behind the operations. “It’s a kind of chain. It’s a supply chain. So, you need to track them. And so NACOC, we have to congratulate NACOC for going through this tangent and making sure that they’re tracking that,” he said on Wednesday, November 4. He added that authorities were picking up individuals suspected of collaborating with the network in Ghana as investigations progressed. The NDC official also appealed to the opposition to allow investigative agencies to carry out their work without political interference. He criticised instances where opposition members allegedly mobilised to investigative bodies following the arrest of persons they considered their associates, claiming such actions could undermine investigations. “The long arm of this investigation will reach out to all those who are involved, who are enabling and who are beneficiaries to this stage,” he said. He maintained that the government’s commitment was to ensure that everyone involved in drug trafficking was brought to account, regardless of their position or role in the network.

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : L’hôpital Sourou Sanou réfute les accusations de refus de soins d’un patient admis en urologie
items.description: Après la diffusion d’une vidéo sur les réseaux sociaux faisant état d’un présumé refus de prise en charge d’un patient au service d’urologie, le Centre hospitalier universitaire Sourô Sanou (CHU-SS) de Bobo-Dioulasso a apporté des éclaircissements. Dans un communiqué publié le 4 novembre 2026, la direction générale indique qu’une enquête interne n’a établi aucun refus de soins imputable à l’établissement. Le Centre hospitalier universitaire Sourô Sanou (CHU-SS) de Bobo-Dioulasso sort du silence après la polémique suscitée par une vidéo diffusée sur les réseaux sociaux, évoquant un présumé refus de prise en charge d’un patient au service d’urologie. À l’issue d’une investigation interne menée du 19 octobre au 2 novembre 2026, la direction générale affirme qu’aucun refus de soins imputable à l’établissement n’a été établi. Dans son communiqué datant de ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, la direction générale précise que le patient concerné bénéficie effectivement d’un suivi médical au sein de l’établissement depuis janvier 2026. Son dossier avait fait l’objet de démarches administratives et médicales auprès du Fonds d’appui à la solidarité nationale (FASSN), qui avait donné son accord pour sa prise en charge. Une intervention chirurgicale reportée en raison de travaux Selon les explications fournies par le CHU Sourô Sanou, l’intervention chirurgicale envisagée n’a toutefois pas pu être réalisée dans ses locaux. En cause : la fermeture temporaire du bloc opératoire concerné, dans le cadre des travaux de réhabilitation de l’établissement. Face à cette situation, et afin d’éviter toute interruption des soins, l’hôpital indique avoir pris les dispositions nécessaires pour orienter le patient vers le Centre hospitalier universitaire Yalgado Ouédraogo (CHU-YO), à Ouagadougou, en collaboration avec le FASSN. La direction générale assure que le patient bénéficie effectivement d’une prise en charge médicale au CHU-YO pour la poursuite de ses soins. Le CHU-SS défend la continuité des soins Au terme de ses investigations, la mission interne n'a donc pas établi de refus de soins imputable au CHU Sourô Sanou. Une conclusion que la direction générale entend opposer aux accusations relayées sur les réseaux sociaux. L’établissement réaffirme, par ailleurs, son engagement à garantir aux usagers un accueil de qualité, une prise en charge adaptée et la continuité des soins, dans le respect de la dignité humaine et de l’équité. Tout en souhaitant un prompt rétablissement au patient, le CHU Sourô Sanou invite les populations à privilégier ses canaux officiels pour toute information relative au fonctionnement de l’établissement. items.title: N50,000 relief fund: FG explains how beneficiaries will be selected
items.description: The Federal Government, FG has outlined how selected poor and vulnerable Nigerian households can receive a ₦50,000 cash grant under its National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI). The programme, implemented by the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, is designed to help vulnerable households cope with rising living costs through direct cash transfers into mobile wallets. According to the programme’s guidelines, beneficiaries will receive the money through designated payment providers, including ALAT, MoMo, NairaGram, OPay and Moniepoint. The government said the intervention uses mobile wallets to ensure that financial support reaches beneficiaries quickly and transparently, with independent checks conducted during each payment cycle. How to receive the FG’s ₦50,000 cash grant The government outlined four steps for selected beneficiaries to access the payment. 1. Receive an SMS notification Selected beneficiaries will receive a text message from one of the designated payment providers informing them that they have been selected for the programme. 2. Confirm participation Recipients are required to reply YES to the message to indicate their consent to participate in the programme. The guidelines state that no payment will be made without the beneficiary’s consent. 3. Activate the mobile wallet Following confirmation, a mobile wallet will be opened and linked to the beneficiary’s phone number and National Identification Number (NIN). 4. Receive and withdraw the money The sum of ₦50,000 will be credited to the beneficiary’s wallet. Recipients can withdraw the money through a Point of Sale (POS) agent, at a bank or spend directly from their mobile wallets. USSD codes to withdraw the ₦50,000 grant Beneficiaries will receive additional SMS instructions from their respective payment providers after their wallets have been credited. The government provided the following withdrawal codes: ALAT (Wema Bank): Dial 94523#. MoMo PSB: Dial 6710#. NairaGram: Dial 72600#. OPay: Dial 95520# or use the mobile application. Moniepoint: Dial 557327# or use the mobile application. How beneficiaries are selected According to the programme’s guidelines, beneficiaries are selected using verified national identity records and the National Social Register. The selection process is designed to identify poor and vulnerable households eligible for the intervention. The government explained that individuals cannot apply independently or pay to be included in the beneficiary list. It also clarified that not everyone will be included in the first group of beneficiaries. FG warns Nigerians against fraud The government cautioned beneficiaries against fraudsters who may attempt to exploit the cash transfer programme by demanding money or personal banking information. It said the programme is free and that nobody is authorised to request payment to facilitate the release of the ₦50,000 grant. The guidelines listed three ways beneficiaries can identify genuine programme messages: Messages must come from ALAT, MoMo, NairaGram, OPay or Moniepoint. Recipients will only be asked to reply YES or dial their payment provider’s designated USSD code. Messages will never request payment, a Personal Identification Number (PIN), a One-Time Password (OTP) or require recipients to click a link. The government also warned beneficiaries against sharing their PINs, OTPs or passwords with anyone, including agents and officials. It advised recipients to ignore messages from unauthorised senders and contact the programme’s helpline if they are unsure about the authenticity of a notification. Frequently asked questions about the NERSI ₦50,000 grant What is NERSI? The National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI) is a Federal Government relief programme designed to help Nigerian households cope with rising living costs. It is implemented by the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction. How much will beneficiaries receive? Each selected beneficiary will receive ₦50,000 in their mobile wallet. The government says the full amount will be credited without deductions. Is the ₦50,000 payment a loan? No. The payment is a Federal Government grant, not a loan, and beneficiaries are not required to repay it. Who is eligible for the cash transfer? Beneficiaries are selected from the National Social Register and verified national identity records. Individuals cannot apply or pay to be included in the list. Those selected will receive an SMS notification from their designated payment provider. Why was I selected, and how did the government obtain my phone number? According to the programme’s guidelines, beneficiaries are selected using information from the National Social Register and verified national identity records. Their phone numbers are obtained from these records and shared only with the relevant payment provider for the purpose of disbursing the grant. The government also stated that beneficiaries’ personal information would be used only for the programme. items.description: By Ahmed Eljechtimi RABAT, Nov 4 (Reuters) - Morocco will stay committed to the ceasefire in Western Sahara despite the end of the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the territory, the Royal Palace said on Wednesday.
